label: Umwelt
summary: Umwelt refers to the species-specific world horizon through which any organism perceives and relates to its environment. As cited in Maaike's reading notes on N. Katherine Hayles, all creatures have umwelten that may overlap but never entirely coincide. The concept is fundamentally incompatible with anthropocentrism because it refuses any single world horizon the right to position itself as the correct or dominant one.
how_maaike_uses: Maaike encounters umwelt primarily as a tool for dismantling anthropocentrism: if every organism has its own world horizon, then the human one loses its claim to be the measure of all others. In her reading notes she pairs the concept directly with the ethical implication that no umwelt has the right to dominate the others, linking it to a broader project of recasting cognition away from human consciousness and toward distributed, nonconscious, and more-than-human cognitive assemblages.
open_questions: If umwelten can overlap but never fully coincide, what does meaningful communication or coordination across them actually look like in practice?
Does the umwelt concept extend to computational media, or does it remain tied to organisms with biological world horizons?
